title: Skills on level up dependant on stats

posts.author: riku5690
posts.body:
So I had this idea for a game, and I wanna know what plugins, common event orders, etc. I could use to make this happen.
lets take 3 player characters, they're the same in player name/class but not in stats.
each of these instances make it to level 5,
player 1's playthrough has a 20 in atk: so he learns a skill that lets him learn a dodge stance.
player 2's playthrough has a 20 in m.def: so he learns a skill that lets him be in a stance that lets him regen mana
player 3's playthrough has a 20 in speed: so he learns a skill that lets him steal
is this possible? I have a theory to simply name the classes the same, have them also change stats but I'm afraid it'll get rid of the skills the player already learned from the other "classes" since skills are gained on level up from the class itself and not the players stats or the player themselves.

Oh, that's a lot different than I thought. That actually simplifies things a lot.
If you want to do this entirely without plugins and are fine with the player knowing this is happening, simply have the character learn a temporary skill at level 5 that calls a Common Event. This event will cause them to learn the correct skill by checking their stats with variables and forcing them to gain a skill. You can further have the event tell them what skill they will learn based on their current stats and even let them back out if there is an option to increase stats in some way (such as with permanent stat increase consumable).

Probably not (no offense, I don't think I could simplify it that far), but I can break things down further;
Make your three skills do whatever you want them to do
Make a fourth skill. This skill can only be used in the menu (under Occasion) and does nothing but call up a Common Event (under Effects)
In the common event, use Control Variables and Conditional Branch to determine the Actor's stats, then Change Skill to add the skill you want them to learn based on those.
To change it to Turan's explanation, don't make the fourth skill and instead make the Common Event a parallel process. You'll need to turn a chosen Switch On at the start of the game that can then be turned Off once the chosen skill is learned.
Utility Common Events (YEP) - Yanfly.moe Wiki
www.yanfly.moe
With the above plugin, you don't need it to be a Parallel Event since the event will be called after each combat and then check for the correct level, stats, etc.
But, again, I
really very much
recommend learning the system more first. Once you are comfortable with the maker, you'll know what it is and is not capable of and where you would need a plugin.

So, to break it down exactly:
First, visit the link to
https://himeworks.com/2015/10/level-up-events/
that Sword_of_Dusk provided above. Download the plugin (in the download section on the site, right click where it tells you to and go Save As). Save the plugin in your plugins folder, in the js folder in your project, add the plugin to your plugin list in game, and make sure it's turned on, in the usual way.
Now, you will need to add a note tag to your actor. Go into your actor in the database, and in the Note section put:
<level up event: COMMON_EVENT_ID>
(Only replace the COMMON_EVENT_ID with a number - this should be the number of the common event that you want to run whenever your actor levels up).
It's now set up so that when this actor levels up, that common event will run. So now you need to set the event up.
This should be easy enough using conditional statements. In your example, you'd want to first check to see if the actor is level 5; if they are, check if they have met the threshold for each stat, and if they have, grant them the appropriate skill. It doesn't look like actor level is one of the default options the Conditional Branch command gives you in the event window, so you'll have to use some script - if you select Conditional Branch, then the last page, in the script window you can type $gameActors.actor(1).level = 5 (or whatever level you're checking). Then you can do another Conditional Branch for checking if the stat is high enough. Note that stats are affected by buffs, equipment, etc, so which command you use to check will vary depending on if you want to include these buffs or not - use:
$gameActors.actor(1).atk to just get actor 1's attack
$gameActors.actor(1).paramBase(2) to get just the base attack value inherited from the class
$gameActors.actor(1)._paramPlus[2] to get their bonus attack from AddParam
$gameActors.actor(1).paramPlus(2) to get their total attack bonus including equipment
(In the last three, the number 2 near the end means attack - for the other stats, the number should be as follows:
Basic parameter IDs:
• 0 = MHP     • 2 = ATK      • 4 = MAT     • 6 = AGI
• 1 = MMP     • 3 = DEF      • 5 = MDF     • 7 = LUK
You can find this information in the
script call Google Doc, here
.)
I'm not sure how the plugin you're using for stat buffs works, but if it's using addParam to increase the stats you might want to use
($gameActors.actor(1).paramBase(2) + $gameActors.actor(1)._paramPlus[2]) >= 10
as your conditional so you don't take the buff the equipment is granting into account, but do include any addParam buffs. Or if you don't care about any of that, just use $gameActors.actor(1).atk >= 10.
Then after the conditionals you could do the Change Skill command to add the right skill to actor 1.
